Twenty-five comments

Paddy Fahey’s Reel

Seems to be about a half dozen Paddy Fahey tunes floating about, but in Dallas, this one is the king of them all. Pick up the Tir Na Nog CD titled Black Rose if you want to hear it properly. This tune lends itself to being played as a slow reel.

↳ Posted by Caoimghgin on December 28th, 2001.

I’m glad that this one has been posted as it’s a favourite of mine and it’s good to hear you like it played slow as that’s my feeling too.

It’s often done a bit too quick for my liking at our local session but it still works and it usually goes into Julia Delaney.
dave

P. Fahey: Reel, Opus 40?

I’ve read that Maestro Fahey numbered his tunes, yet I rarely see them referred to by number. Why is this? Wouldn’t it be a lot easier to talk about them if we didn’t have to say, “you know, the one that goes ta da diddley diddley do”? I put in a request here for one of the reels and the only way I could refer to it was by its track position on a specific recording.

Is there a list somewhere that ties tune to number?

↳ Posted by Bob himself on September 5th, 2005.

Paddy Fahey’s, X:8

Only slight differences here in this version, I suppose, but somehow all the more satisfying to my ear because of them. I love that this tune includes all four strings on the fiddle. The dark, gutsy low start to the tune is quickly elevated to the high “A” on the E string, and is further tempered playful phrases and rocking between strings. As much fun to listen to as to play.

Paddy Fahey’s, X:13

Trying to play X:12 I had some ideas how to put it on the flute I would like to share.
I tried to avoid the notes below D and to reduce the fnat to make it easier to play.
The FFF is played like a cran ( F{G}F{A}F ) and can be played only if your flute has a Fnat key.

↳ Posted by swisspiper on May 7th, 2025.

Paddy Fahey’s, X:14

This the transcription that appears in Maria Holohan’s thesis on Paddy Fahey’s life and compositions, which in turn comes from his own playing of the tune. It might not be proper to call it the “original” version since he himself may have varied it at times, but this is at least how the composer had it on that day.
